# 🌙 The Midnight Buildathon
![Image](https://res.cloudinary.com/travary/image/upload/w_800/v1/prd-akindo-public/wave-hacks/description-images/9340nNWW7cW0mlZP.png)
## A Three-Wave Builder Program for Privacy-First Apps

---

> ### 🚀 Wave 1 Opens August 27
>
> **Registration is open now.** Wave 1 build period starts **August 27, 2026 at 12:00 AM JST**.
>
> 💬 **Builder support runs on the Midnight Discord.**
> Technical questions, program updates, and direct access to the Midnight team.
> 👉 **[Join the Discord →](https://discord.gg/SUZNRF6fu)**

---

 ### 🎥 Start Here: Kickoff Workshop (Online)
 **New to Midnight? Start with the workshop.**

<iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/_zT--UCqxh8" width="560" height="315"></iframe>


---

### ✨ About the Program

The Midnight Buildathon is a three-month online builder program hosted on AKINDO for teams creating privacy-first applications.

Instead of treating the experience as a one-shot competition, the program is designed around **three connected Waves**. Teams are expected to build, submit, learn, improve, and return with stronger work each time.

The core idea is simple: **progress, iteration, and sustained participation matter more than one-time polish**.

This is a **progress-driven Buildathon** for builders who want to turn an early concept into a stronger product direction, stronger implementation, and stronger ecosystem fit over time.

---

### 🌑 What Is Midnight?

Midnight is a next-generation blockchain built for developers who want to protect user and business data while building open, verifiable applications.

It combines public transparency with programmable data protection and selective disclosure, enabling developers to prove facts without revealing private information.

#### Why Midnight?

**For Business:**

- **Finance** – Prove solvency, transaction validity, or compliance requirements without disclosing balances or counterparties.
- **AI** – Prove model integrity or dataset origin without revealing the underlying content.
- **Gaming** – Verify player actions or game logic privately on-chain.
- **Healthcare** – Enable access to facts about data, such as “record verified” or “treatment completed,” without revealing the underlying medical data.
- **Governance** – Prove eligibility or participation without exposing identity.
- **Identity** – Issue credentials that users can verify privately.

**For Developers:**

- **Learnable** – Write contracts in TypeScript using Compact, Midnight’s privacy-enabled smart-contract language that abstracts zero-knowledge complexity.
- **Composable** – Integrate seamlessly with TypeScript SDKs.
- **Flexible** – Choose what to disclose, including full data, selected information, or hashed attestations.
- **Interoperable** – Built to connect with other ecosystems, beginning with Cardano.

---

### 🚀 Why Join the Midnight Buildathon?

This program is for builders who want more than a final score.

Why teams should join:

- Build across multiple Waves instead of a single deadline.
- Show real progress and product refinement over time.
- Receive comments and feedback on submissions.
- Stay visible to the community throughout the program.
- Test privacy-first ideas in a practical environment.
- Learn faster through builder-facing guidance, onboarding, and feedback loops.
- Earn potential showcase opportunities for strong projects.
- Continue improving the same project and demonstrate what changed in each Wave.
- Get direct support from the Midnight team through the official Discord throughout the program.

**Start with the kickoff workshop** — meet the Midnight team live and learn what judges look for before Wave 1 opens. [Register here →](https://luma.com/midnight-buildathon)

---

### 📦 What We Look For

Teams should submit a project that is clearly aligned with the privacy-first theme and shows meaningful progress during each Wave in which they participate.

At a minimum, submissions should:

- Present a product, prototype, developer tool, infrastructure solution, or working concept related to the theme.
- Explain how privacy meaningfully shapes the product or technical design.
- Communicate the current state of the project clearly.
- Reflect iteration, refinement, or advancement where relevant.
- Show what changed since the previous Wave when continuing with the same project.
- Include evidence of testing, validation, traction, or real use cases when available.
- Include a clear demo, walkthrough, or equivalent proof of progress where relevant.
- Include technical or architectural information where it helps judges understand the privacy design and Midnight integration.
- Meet the technical, licensing, and submission requirements described below.

Please refer to the Rules section to find out what you need to submit.

---

### 🌊 Program Structure

The Midnight Buildathon runs as a **3-Wave program from August 27, 2026 to November 27, 2026**.

| Wave | Build Period | Judging Period | Reward |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| **Wave 1** | **August 27 – September 16, 2026** | **September 16 – September 27, 2026** | **US$3,500** |
| **Wave 2** | **September 27 – October 17, 2026** | **October 17 – October 27, 2026** | **US$4,000** |
| **Wave 3** | **October 27 – November 16, 2026** | **November 16 – November 27, 2026** | **US$5,000** |

The specific Submission Deadline time for each Wave will be displayed on the AKINDO platform and in the Official Rules.

Only the version submitted by the applicable Submission Deadline will be considered in the evaluation of that Wave. Teams may continue developing their projects after the deadline, but subsequent changes will not be considered for that Wave and may instead be submitted in a later Wave.

This repeating build-and-evaluation rhythm is designed to reward teams that keep shipping, learning, and refining instead of waiting for a single final reveal.

*Dates may be adjusted by mutual agreement based on participant momentum.*

---

### 📏 Rules

Fully virtual, August 27 – November 27, 2026. A Buildathon in three Waves on the most ambitious privacy network of the new generation. Read carefully before applying.

**These rules are a summary.** The binding, official document is the contest's *Official Rules*. In case of any discrepancy, the Official Rules prevail: **[[RULES PDF LINK](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YKXtsw5nghcEBEW0BFrLn-U34AfH_MF4/view?usp=sharing)]**

#### 1. Teams

- Teams may consist of up to **five (5) registered members**.
- If entering as a team, every team member must register individually through the AKINDO platform.
- A team must identify the members associated with each submission.
- Any internal allocation of a Development Grant among team members is the sole responsibility of the team unless otherwise stated in the Official Rules.

#### 2. Project Development and Open-Source Requirements

Existing products, frameworks, libraries, and codebases may be used.

However, the Midnight-related functionality submitted for evaluation must be **newly developed or materially extended during the applicable Wave**.

Projects submitted in an earlier Wave may be further developed and resubmitted in a later Wave, provided that the later submission demonstrates meaningful new progress completed during that Wave.

Mere copies, superficial modifications, or submissions that do not demonstrate meaningful new Midnight-related functionality are not eligible.

The Midnight-related code newly developed or materially extended for the Buildathon, including the submitted Compact contract and code reasonably necessary to evaluate its functionality, must be publicly available under the **Apache License 2.0**.

Pre-existing or independently developed code may remain subject to its existing license, provided that judges can access and evaluate the Midnight-related functionality required for the submission.

#### 3. Eligibility

- You must be **18 years of age or older** as of the date of entry.
- Individuals or entities located in — or holding a wallet that has transacted in — any sanctioned jurisdiction subject to sanctions administered or enforced by the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control, the United Nations Security Council, the European Union, His Majesty’s Treasury’s Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation, or another relevant sanctions authority are not eligible.
- Residents of Afghanistan, Belarus, Cuba, Iran, Iraq, North Korea, Russia, Syria, Venezuela, Yemen, Myanmar, Somalia, or Sudan are also excluded.
- Anyone participating as a **volunteer, judge, or in another privileged role** is not eligible to compete.
- Officers, directors, and employees of the Sponsor, Midnight Foundation, and related entities, together with their immediate family members and household members, may participate but are **not eligible to win prizes or receive Development Grants**.

Full eligibility details are set out in the Official Rules.

#### 4. Registration and Entry

- This is an **open event**. All eligible individuals who register through this AKINDO Program page may participate.
- If entering as a team, **every team member must register individually**.
- Entries must be submitted personally by the entrant or registered team members.
- Automated entry tools are prohibited.
- The use of multiple AKINDO, Discord, and/or Telegram accounts to submit duplicate entries, misrepresent an entrant’s identity, or otherwise circumvent the Official Rules is prohibited.
- Entries will be deemed submitted by the authorized holder of the AKINDO account used for the submission.
- Entrants may be required to verify ownership of any AKINDO, Discord, or Telegram account identified in connection with their entry.

#### 5. Format and Schedule

The Buildathon is **fully virtual**, running from **August 27 to November 27, 2026**.

The Contest Period is divided into three connected Waves:

| Wave | Build Period | Judging Period |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Wave 1** | August 27 – September 16, 2026 | September 16 – September 27, 2026 |
| **Wave 2** | September 27 – October 17, 2026 | October 17 – October 27, 2026 |
| **Wave 3** | October 27 – November 16, 2026 | November 16 – November 27, 2026 |

The end of each Build Period is the applicable **Submission Deadline**.

Only the version submitted by the applicable Submission Deadline will be considered for that Wave. Teams may continue development after the deadline, but later changes will not affect the evaluation of that Wave.

Later changes may be submitted in a subsequent Wave, provided that the submission demonstrates meaningful new progress.

Teams may participate in one or more Waves unless otherwise specified in the Official Rules.

#### 6. Submission Requirements

By the applicable Submission Deadline, each team must submit the following through **the submission page on the AKINDO platform**:

- A link to a publicly accessible **GitHub repository** containing the relevant project code and related files.
- A clear **README** explaining the project, setup process, architecture, Midnight integration, and how judges can test or evaluate the submission.
- A **slide deck ** (pitch presentation).
- A **demo / video pitch**.
- A description of the progress completed during the applicable Wave.
- When resubmitting a project from an earlier Wave, a clear explanation of what has changed since the previous submission.

The repository must include the **`midnightntwrk` label on GitHub**.

The submitted Midnight-related code must comply with the Apache License 2.0 requirements described above.

Forks and existing codebases may be used only where the submission introduces meaningful new functionality or material improvements related to Midnight. Mere copies or minor modifications are not eligible.

If selected or requested by the judges, the team must also participate in a live presentation or interview at a time communicated to the team in advance.

#### 7. Judging and Evaluation

All eligible submissions will be evaluated under the official Midnight Buildathon Judging Rubric.

| Criterion | Weight |
| --- | ---: |
| **Engineering & Implementation** — Evaluates whether the Compact contract compiles, includes private-state management, and demonstrates an understanding of Midnight’s dual-ledger model. The repository should be well organized with a clear README. We encourage participants to tag their repositories with relevant Midnight topics and include ecosystem attribution. | **40%** |
| **Quality Assurance & Reliability** — Evaluates the presence of simulation and test files, whether test cases pass, and the overall stability of the product under basic use. | **15%** |
| **Product & Vision** — Evaluates the strength of the idea, its connection to Midnight’s core capabilities, and whether its scope and roadmap are realistic. | **15%** |
| **User Experience & Design** — Evaluates whether the frontend is intuitive, behaves as expected, and connects to the contract as part of a functional end-to-end experience. | **15%** |
| **Communication** — Evaluates the clarity and structure of the video presentation and slide deck. | **10%** |
| **Business Development & Viability** — Evaluates awareness of the target audience, market potential, and the proposed adoption path. | **5%** |

#### Technical Gate

Each submission must include at least one Compact contract that compiles successfully.

A submission that does not satisfy this requirement will be automatically disqualified from judging for the applicable Wave.

To be eligible for judging, each project must:

- Include at least one Compact contract that compiles successfully.
- Provide meaningful Midnight-related functionality.
- Not be a mere fork, copy, or superficial modification of an existing project.
- Include the `midnightntwrk` label on GitHub.
- Include a public GitHub repository, slide deck, and demo video or video pitch.
- Satisfy the applicable licensing, eligibility, and submission requirements.

Participants may view the points assigned by the judges on the AKINDO platform during the judging period, including in real time where available.

View the full judging rubric here:

[Midnight Buildathon Judging Rubric](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-dDTqWa2CcfnSEvgXq83La2M8zAxi4jtVtKpMJRm3Oo/edit?usp=sharing)

#### 8. Grants

The Development Grant Pool allocated to each Wave will be distributed among eligible submissions in proportion to the points they receive during the judging process for that Wave.

| Wave | Development Grant Pool |
| --- | ---: |
| **Wave 1** | **US$3,500** |
| **Wave 2** | **US$4,000** |
| **Wave 3** | **US$5,000** |
| **Total** | **US$12,500** |

Development Grants will be made available for distribution as soon as reasonably practicable following the end of the judging period for the applicable Wave, subject to eligibility verification, compliance checks, and funding availability.

Receiving a Development Grant in one Wave does not prevent a team from participating in a later Wave, provided that its later submission complies with the Official Rules and demonstrates meaningful new progress.

Participants are responsible for all taxes associated with the acceptance of any prize or Development Grant.

#### 9. Midnight Build Club

Teams selected by the judges are eligible to join the Midnight Build Club. All members of each selected team have access to the program.

**About the Midnight Build Club:** The Midnight Build Club is an eight-week, part-time educational program for high-potential, idea-stage projects.

Teams learn from senior experts in software development, business development, and marketing strategy and are guided, with an extensive suite of tools and resources, through validating and refining their ideas and developing a strong foundation for their startups.

At the end of the program, teams have the opportunity to pitch to Midnight’s network of investors for funding and acceptance into the Midnight Accelerator Program.

The total Approximate Retail Value (ARV) of all prizes is **US$12,500** plus the value of the Midnight Build Club program. Actual value may vary based on market conditions. Winners are responsible for all taxes associated with acceptance of any prize.

---

### 🧭 How to Join

1. **Register Now**  
   Sign up on AKINDO and join the Midnight Buildathon page.

2. **Register Every Team Member**  
   Each member of a participating team must register individually.

3. **Join the Midnight Discord** 💬  
   The Midnight Discord is the main support channel for this Buildathon. Technical questions, builder support, program updates, and direct access to the Midnight team all happen there.

   👉 **[Join the Midnight Discord →](https://discord.gg/SUZNRF6fu)**

   Head to the Buildathon channel once you're in. This is where you'll get help fastest.

4. **Attend the Kickoff Workshop** 🎥  
   Join the online kickoff session the night before Wave 1 opens. Meet the Midnight team, get a walkthrough of the tech, see exactly what judges score, and ask anything in the live Q&A.

   **📅 August 26, 2026 · 10:00 PM JST (1:00 PM UTC) · Online · Free**

   A recording will be shared afterward.

   👉 **[Register on Luma →](https://luma.com/midnight-buildathon)**

5. **Build, Submit, and Iterate**  
   Build during each Wave, submit your progress, get evaluated, and keep improving. The Program is designed to reward teams that continue sharpening their products across all three Waves.

Early teams usually benefit more, because they have more time to participate across all Waves, absorb feedback sooner, and build momentum inside the Program.

---

- [Midnight docs](https://docs.midnight.network/)

- [Kapa and Midnight Expert MCP server](https://docs.midnight.network/blog/migrating-to-kapa-and-midnight-expert) – Code smart contracts and dapps with AI
